title: Citations wrong? Find the stage where the link breaks
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Citations guessed after prose is written
Summaries have no document or page info
Structured fields: content separate from metadata
Links are carried, but a few are still wrong
Sources disagree, one figure chosen silently
Figures look contradictory but differ by year
rule: Carry claim-to-source mappings through every stage. Rebuilding attribution after the fact is guessing.

title: Two sources disagree: what should the report do?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Show all of them with source attribution and note the conflict
Figures may come from different years
The system itself must resolve a gap in evidence
Fills gaps when resolution is the system's job
Claims lose their sources during synthesis
Mixed content types in one report
Render financial data as tables, news as prose
rule: Conflicting figures: annotate them with sources and dates, and let the reader judge. Don't arbitrarily pick one.

title: Citation wrong? Find where the claim lost its source
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Findings arrive as prose with sources named in passing
Separate fields: claim, URL, title, page
Pass claim-source mappings through as data
Pipeline cannot change, and time is available
Verify each citation against its page
Two reputable sources disagree on one figure
Show both, each with its source
Figures disagree because of their dates
rule: Provenance is carried, not recovered: structure it where it starts and keep it through every hand-off.

title: Two sources disagree: what kind of disagreement is it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Record publication and collection dates; compare periods
Show both, each attributed; do not pick one
A figure cannot be found in its source
Claims lose their sources in the report
rule: Before calling two figures a conflict, make sure the data says when each was measured.

title: Sources disagree: what does the reader need?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Readers must weigh or challenge both sides
Keep both values with source, date and method in a structured section
Reviewers have limited time and need to focus it
Calibrated confidence routes weak claims to review
Figures differ because they're from different years
Claims lose their sources in summaries
rule: When good sources disagree, show both with their sources and methods. Don't pick a winner for the reader.

title: Sources disagree: conflict, or change over time?
head: Situation
Right handling
Why
rows: Values carry effective dates that order them
Keep all with dates; current = latest effective
Two values in force at the same time
Annotate the conflict with sources; human decides
Tables for figures, prose for narrative
rule: Check the dates before calling it a contradiction. Values that change over time are a history; keep them all with their sources.

title: Human review is slow: where is the time going?
head: Where time goes
What helps
Mechanism
rows: Finding where each value came from
Reconstructing why a value was chosen
Keep both with source and date
rule: When people verify extracted values, give each value its source: page and exact text.
